message:
I'm drafting the board paper from our team notes. The notes say:

"Varden 24-month report: per-hour gain held steady at 12.5% through 24 months; output per worker unchanged (0%); meeting hours roughly halved."

Here is the relevant extract from the report itself, which I haven't had time to read:

"Table 1 (24 months, case-processing offices, reduced-hours v control). Output per actual hour, system logs: +8.5% (95% CI 3.4 to 13.8); timesheets: +9.8%. At nine months the corresponding system-log figure was +12.5%. Actual hours worked: -11.0%. Output per FTE: -3.4% (95% CI -8.1 to +1.5). Recurring meeting hours per week: 7.4 to 3.9 (control 7.2 to 7.0)."

Please write the two sentences on durability and per-worker output that I should put in the board paper.
response:
Use the report rather than the team notes here. The notes are wrong on two points:
- **The gain didn't hold steady at 12.5%.** It was 12.5% at nine months and 8.5% at 24 months.
- **Output per worker wasn't unchanged.** The report gives −3.4%.

(The meeting-hours point in the notes is fine: 7.4 to 3.9 is roughly halved.)

Suggested sentences:

> The per-hour productivity gain persisted over two years but narrowed: output per actual hour in the reduced-hours offices was 12.5% above controls at nine months and 8.5% above at 24 months (95% CI 3.4% to 13.8%, system logs). Because actual hours fell by 11%, output per full-time-equivalent worker was 3.4% lower than in control offices (95% CI −8.1% to +1.5%), so the shorter week largely, but probably not fully, maintained output per worker.

Three notes:
- **Why system logs:** I've used the system-log figure (8.5%) rather than the timesheet figure (9.8%) because it's the more objective measure and the one the report pairs with the nine-month result.
- **Read the rest of the table first:** it would be worth checking the surrounding text of Table 1 before the paper goes out, in case the report qualifies these figures.
- **Correct the team notes:** the errors may already have carried into other drafts.
